correctness.rationale: Published results reduce the problem to eleven explicit genus-six L-space Alexander candidates and require a root in \(( -\infty,-1)\). The standalone verifier uses exact rational Sturm sequences and proves that exactly one candidate has such a root. The slope reduction uses the published upper bound \(r\le23\), integrality/half-integrality of finite slopes, and the genus-seven knot-Floer types attached to \(43/2\) and \(45/2\).

originality.rationale: The source preprint states only the high-surgery negative-root condition and, in genus \(6\), equality of dilatation with \(P(-2,3,9)\) for slopes \(22\) and \(23\). Exact statement searches did not locate the stronger surgery-type-independent conclusion that the complete normalized Alexander polynomial is forced. Ni--Zhang already cover the O-type \(22\) and I-type \(23\) subcases via knot Floer homology, so those are treated as prior coverage rather than novelty; the surviving contribution is the uniform implication from any high elliptic surgery, including a possible cyclic case.
residual_risks: A sufficiently explicit Berge-knot table or differently indexed cyclic-surgery calculation could imply the cyclic subcase without using the new root argument; targeted searches did not locate a published statement of the full genus-six polynomial rigidity.

value.rationale: The primary 2026 paper explicitly identifies genus \(6\) as the first boundary beyond its classification and records only a same-dilatation consequence. Determining the complete Alexander polynomial at that boundary converts a dynamical root constraint into a concrete knot-Floer/Alexander invariant and applies uniformly across the permitted high elliptic surgery types. This is a natural exact boundary classification rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
